kernels.method: Five fixed geometries at 256 and 400 image cells per side, both phases. Four rotating policy orders; 16 calls per timer. Loading, warmups, backend calibration and coordinate equality checks are outside the timers. Every timed result must match the previous gradient exactly. Times are milliseconds per call.

report.method: Five fixed geometries at 256 and 400 image cells per side, both phases. Four rotating policy orders; 16 calls per timer. Loading, warmups, backend calibration and coordinate equality checks are outside the timers. Every timed result must match the previous gradient exactly. Times are milliseconds per call.

hunodan.criteria: Each prepare + solve + validate + export <=10 seconds; independent error <= that case’s validated release error, plus at most 1 percentage point for an identical pair; unchanged geometry, strict paper and substantial feature checks. Decode and independent external replay are timed separately.

hunodanReplay.note: Separate fresh process after the complete Node checks, with calibration included. Does not replace the original full-batch result.

weighted.method: Fresh automatic mask solves. Frames fixed before fitting. Checker strategy replaces the band; weighted strategy retains the original mask with zero band weights. Exported controls are independently rendered with resvg. Geometric and paper checks remain enabled. Variants swap both colours, translate by one source pixel in both axes with background fill, or alter only zero-weight pixels; the protected frame stays fixed.

limitations: Exact coordinate equality is checked on the recorded inputs; it is not a proof for every future geometry or browser runtime.
Timed gradient comparisons exclude calibration and warmup. Whole-solve replays include their normal initialization and calibration.
The whole-solve batches are separate runs, not alternating comparisons. Speed depends on runtime and hardware, and fitting remains deadline-dependent.
Workload buckets select a measured implementation; timing on one geometry cannot guarantee optimal speed for every later geometry in the same bucket.
The guarded discrete paper model does not certify tear resistance or physical assembly.
